column4: D_frame_state_pairs — the JDK gates this write behind isFrameStateSupported, and a browser supports no frame state, so NORMAL is the faithful answer. The oracle disagrees only because it runs under a window manager.

R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) — L&F dispatch is permanently out of scope, so there is no class to fail to load.
R_layouts_close_enough — the JDK answers -5 / -2 here, which is unlaid-out pixel arithmetic rather than a contract worth reproducing.
R_layouts_close_enough — dummy bounds are stated policy; no server-side geometry exists to answer with. D_pixel_layout_not_planned.
R_layouts_close_enough — as Component.Bounds; the frame renders as a Dialog overlay that sizes itself (D_internal_frames).

R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) — the JDK's answer here is a BasicInternalFrameUI$Handler, i.e. the L&F's own layout manager installed by the UI, and setLayout redirects to the content pane on both layers. With no UI there is nothing to answer but null.

D_jfilechooser_park — getCurrentDirectory round-trips its field because there is no server FS browse. The JDK's body validates against a real filesystem (a dir that does not exist reverts to the previous one, then walks up to a traversable parent), which would make the answer depend on the box the app is deployed on for a chooser whose picker is the browser's.
